name: Hero MotoCorp Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest two-wheeler maker by volume (Oct 2026 dispatches 7.34 lakh, +16% y/y), focused on entry commuter motorcycles and scooters (Splendor, HF Deluxe, Xoom, Destini), with a premium push (Xtreme, Karizma, Harley partnership) and an EV arm VIDA (retail 66,000 units in Q2 FY27, gross-margin positive). Debt-free, ~71% dividend payout (3.4% yield). Holds an associate stake in Ather Energy. Exports (Latin America, Bangladesh, Africa) are ~6% of sales. Rural and semi-urban demand, financing availability and commodity costs drive earnings.

exposures.mechanism: Steel ~12% of sales (model estimate). +7% -> +0.84% of sales; EBITDA margin 13% -> -6.5% pre pass-through; ~50% recovered through 'judicious price action' (CFO, 2026-10-29) -> -3.2%; EV/MCap ~0.95 (net cash), persistence 0.4 -> -1.2. No significant pack sensitivity (global HRC not in top 12).

evidence.note: CFO: input cost inflation persists in Q3; offset by cost savings, VIDA economics and selective price rises

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium (engines, wheels, castings) ~7% of sales. +10% -> 0.7% of sales -> EBITDA -5.4% pre; 50% passed on -> -2.7%; x0.95 x0.4 = -1.0. Agrees with pack empirical -1.04 per +10% (t -1.3). Aluminium is -19.6% since 2026-06-01 (factor_state), a tailwind for H2.

Copper (harness, motors, EV drivetrain) ~2% of sales; +10% -> 0.2% of sales -> EBITDA -1.5% pre; 50% recovery; x0.95 x0.4 = -0.3. Pack empirical -0.64 (t -0.9) points the same way but is larger/insignificant.
Tyres ~3.5% of sales; rubber ~half of tyre cost -> 1.7% of sales; +10% -> -1.3% EBITDA pre; 50% recovered; x0.95 x0.4 = -0.25. Rubber RSS4 +62% y/y (Mint 2026-11-05) so mostly already in Q2 costs.

evidence.note: RSS4 rubber +62% y/y, tyre price hikes

exposures.mechanism: Direct channel: plastics, paint, lubricants, freight and fuel cost of ownership for a fuel-price-sensitive commuter buyer. +10% Brent -> ~0.3% of sales cost -> EBITDA -2% pre; 50% passed; x0.95 x0.4 = -0.4 plus ~-0.2 sentiment. Partial offset: higher petrol prices help VIDA EV demand (retail +80% y/y in Oct). Pack empirical Brent not in top 12 (not significant).

evidence.note: CFO attributes input cost inflation to extended West Asia conflict

exposures.mechanism: Pack empirical -6.27 per +3% USD/CNY (t -3.5, the only significant factor). Plausible channel: weaker yuan lowers prices of Chinese electronics, EV components and magnets Hero imports/competes with and signals easing Asian cost pressure (inverse: yuan strength raises input cost). Weight shrunk to about one third of the empirical estimate because the link is partly a regime/sentiment proxy. Low confidence.

Exports ~6% of sales (Colombia, Bangladesh, Africa) vs imported electronics/EV parts and some commodities ~8% of costs: net import-long. +3% -> costs +0.24% of sales (-1.8% EBITDA) vs export gain +0.18% -> net ~-0.5% EBITDA x0.95 plus sentiment ... rounded -1.0 incl. empirical -1.61 per +3% (t -1.1) blend.

+10% industry 2W volumes -> Hero volume +10%; contribution margin ~22% vs EBITDA margin 13% -> gearing 1.7x -> EBITDA +17%; x0.95 x persistence 0.3 = +4.8; rounded +4.5. Oct 2026 dispatches 7.34 lakh (+16%), Q2 revenue +23%; market-share target 14%.

evidence.note: Auto sector rally on easing crude

exposures.mechanism: ~55-60% of Hero entry-commuter volumes are rural/semi-urban (model knowledge). +5pp rural growth -> volume +3% -> EBITDA +5% x0.95 x0.3 = +1.4. Partly overlaps F_AUTO_DEMAND_IN; kept smaller.

evidence.note: No rural-specific disclosure fetched; model knowledge

exposures.mechanism: 2W buyers are the most credit-sensitive vehicle segment (~60-65% financed by NBFCs at high rates - model knowledge). +25bp -> volume -0.4%, EBITDA -0.7% pre -> x0.95 x0.5 = -0.3; plus multiple compression on a 18x P/E stock ~-0.4 = -0.7. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07.

VIDA retail 66,000 units in Q2 (+74% y/y), gross-margin positive, EBITDA drag cut to Rs 168 cr from Rs 232 cr; stronger EV support improves VIDA unit economics and PLI accruals (Rs 63 cr in Q2, ~3% of quarterly EBITDA), but accelerates the ICE core's substitution risk (Elara: entry-level reset as low-speed EVs gain ground - headline 2026-09-28). Net +0.8.

evidence.note: VIDA gross-margin positive, 66,000 retail units, Rs 63 cr PLI accrual in Q2 FY27

exposures.mechanism: EV PLI accrual Rs 63 cr in Q2 FY27 = 3.2% of Q2 EBITDA (Rs 1,997 cr). +1 (expansion/disbursement) -> +25-50% accruals -> +1-1.5% EBITDA x0.95 x0.5 -> ~+0.8.

evidence.note: Rs 63 cr EV PLI accruals recognised in Q2

exposures.mechanism: Direct logistics channel: management said West Asia-linked logistics disruption hit shipments to Colombia and Bangladesh; exports ~6% of sales, expected to return to double-digit growth in Q3/Q4. +1 escalation -> export volume -15% for 2 quarters -> -0.9% of sales... EBITDA -2.5% x0.95 x0.3 = -0.7. Commodity channel is on other edges.

evidence.note: Exports hit by logistics disruption; recovery expected in Q3/Q4

current_state.trend: Revenue Rs 14,970 cr (+23% y/y), EBITDA Rs 1,997 cr (13.3% vs 14.5% a year ago), reported PAT Rs 1,861 cr (+41%) including Rs 397 cr one-time gain; underlying PAT ~Rs 1,456 cr (+5%), a miss vs estimates (CNBC TV18). Shares fell ~4% on 2026-10-29. Management guides Q3 margin 'stable' despite continued input inflation and expects exports to return to double-digit growth.
